An upper body profile vignetted portrait of a Dinka girl wearing earrings and neck ornaments, her hair closely braided.

A Dinka man setting out towards a game path with an animal trap (dang) on his back, consisting of a wooden frame with rope [poor image]. The Powell-Cotton's collected this trap, perhaps from the individual in this image, on the 3rd May 1933, and donated it to the Pitt Rivers Museum. It is likely that this print is a still taken from the cine-film made by Powell-Cotton during this expedition.

A Dinka man setting an animal trap (dang) into the earth on a game path [poor image]. The Powell-Cotton's collected this trap, perhaps from the individual in this image, on the 3rd May 1933, and donated it to the Pitt Rivers Museum. It is likely that this print is a still taken from the cine-film made by Powell-Cotton during this expedition.

A close up of a Dinka man setting an animal trap (dang) on a game path, creating rope tension in the bow section. The Powell-Cotton's collected this trap, perhaps from the individual in this image, on the 3rd May 1933, and donated it to the Pitt Rivers Museum in 1934. It is likely that this print is a still taken from the cine-film made by Powell-Cotton during this expedition.

A man wearing a body cloth sits on his haunches on a neat gravel path edged with stones, probably around the American Mission at Nasir, which Evans-Pritchard revisited during his short period of fieldwork in 1935. Evans-Pritchard notes that this man is probably a Dinka.
A head and shoulders full face portrait of a man on the bank of the Sobat River wearing a European shirt, showing distinctive Dinka V-shape initiation scars on his forehead.
A poorly focussed portrait of a Dinka man wearing a checked body cloth, with a steamer wood station just beyond him.
An upper body full face portrait of a man wearing a European shirt and checked textile body wrap. Evans-Pritchard notes that this man is a Dinka.

A male and female dancer, probably Dinka, in close dancing formation. The man is wearing a feather in his hair, a wide beaded waist band with a small band of probably leopard fur below, a wooden disk arm ornament and is holding a club. The woman, who is stretching her arms back as part of her dance movement, is wearing a long apron, probably goat skin, fringed with beads, as well as cowrie waist bands. Just beyond the pair another pair are dancing together, the male holding his spear aloft. This image resembles several taken of Dinka dances by Godfrey Lienhardt (see for instance 2005.51.427), and may have been given to Evans-Pritchard by him. [CM 17/07/2006]

A man marking dark lines on the ash-smeared shaven heads of three girls to guide the scarification knife. Lienhardt (whose Dinka ox-name was Thienydeng) describes having been taken to witness this event by a master of the fishing-spear, who after seeing the blood produced retired to a distance, claiming that the sight of blood weakened the Flesh divinity within him.
A hand-coloured postcard portrait of a Dinka man wearing bead ornaments, body cloth tied at the shoulder and feather plumes in his hair.
A full length group postcard portrait of four women and a girl holding baskets and other containers on their heads, described as living in the 'Forest of Bor'.
Houses of returned Internally Displaced Persons at Leweng village.
People meeting to discuss local welfare issues.

People meeting to discuss local welfare issues. In the foreground a man is holding up something that a child found in the bush and was playing with - part of a rocket-propelled grenade. Two United Nations men who were escorting Moro are visible to the right.
An elderly Dinka woman at Paloich making food in her dwelling area.
A granary or sleeping hut within a homestead raised on piles.

A group of possibly Dinka men, with some others wearing Arab dress, gathered in front of the camera. The location is probably also in Southern Kordofan region, taken as Thesiger was making his way to Kutum and Tibesti in July 1938.
A large group of Dinka dancing, with a woman wearing a white textile headdress visible in the foreground.

A large group of Dinka youths gathered at a dance, with men in the foreground wearing dancing aprons and holding numerous dancing sticks. Two men to the right are wearing metal armrings on their left arm.
A large group of Dinka youths gathered at a dance, with a line of youths in the foreground holding their arms and spears in the air. They all wear short dance aprons of differing sorts.
A large group of Dinka youths gathered at a dance, with a youth dancing at close quarters in the foreground wearing a lion cloth.
A large group of Dinka youths gathered at a dance, with a youth dancing at close quarters in the foreground wearing armrings and a head cloth, holding a spear in his left hand.
A large group of Dinka youths gathered at a dance, holding long spears over their shoulders, some wearing head cloths.
A large group of Dinka youths gathered at a dance, with girls in the foreground wearing short dancing aprons.
A dark image of a gathering of Dinka youths dancing. In the background is the tall metal pole seen in other images from this dance ground.

A full length portrait of a Dinka man wearing European-style shirt and shorts. Beyond is a large open-sided shelter with men gathered. A hat and rifle lie on the ground next to the shelter, and a locally made bed is also just visible beyond the standing figure.

A portrait of four adolescent Dinka girls, a mother with a baby, and other bystanders, in a public area near a large brick-built rectilinear building with extended thatch verandah. Just visible behind them are an Arab trader and a bicycle.

A portrait of a Dinka man wearing shirt and shorts, smoking a pipe. He is sitting on the brick foundation of a building with mesh windows, used as a backdrop to a number of Dinka portraits taken by Lienhardt.
A profile head-and-shoulders portrait of a Dinka man wearing a textile wrap smoking a cigarette.
A Dinka youth wearing shorts playing a hide-covered drum with a wooden beater at a dance gathering, whilst an older youth plays the larger drum to the right.
A group of Dinka youths sitting in and around the entrance to Lienhardt's canvas tent, one holding a magazine (entitled 'illustrated') which features a white girl with a dog on the cover.
A portrait of a seated Dinka youth wearing a textile hair covering, metal arm rings, and various ornaments strung on a string round the neck.
An upper body portrait of Dinka youth wearing a textile hair covering and large ivory arm band, standing near a field of millet.
An upper body portrait of Dinka youth wearing a textile hair covering and numerous fine strings of beads gathered through a large bead.

A group of four women wearing textile body cloths and beads on a path, perhaps having just met, with one drinking water from a metal bowl, the other with her hand underneath as if to support the bowl.
Dinka youths and girls dancing with dance sticks and whistles. In the background is the tall metal pole seen in other images from this dance ground.

A three-quarter length portrait of two Dinka women wearing animal skin, strings of beads around the waist and coiled metal armbands, lip ring and pendants braided into the hair on the forehead, with a youth wearing similar beads and holding a club standing alongside them.
An upper body portrait of a Dinka youth with arms folded.
A Dinka woman wearing skin apron and a large necklet consisting of strings of beads, standing in grassland.
A group of three Dinka youths standing near a hearth with a kettle near it, outside an open-sided long rectilinear thatched building with spears leaning against the roof.
A dark image of two Dinka youths standing on a steep river bank.
Looking from the deck of a river boat towards a west-bank fishing settlement on the Nile, between Juba and Adok, probably a Dinka fishing village.
Cattle tethered at a cattle camp with matting, gourd vessels and spears in the foreground, resting against a forked tree.
A three-quarter length portrait of a Dinka youth in European shirt and shorts.
Looking across a crowd of Dinka people watching a parade of children (out of frame, seen in related images), with a drummer in the foreground.
A Dinka youth with leprosy showing his affected arms to the camera.
An upper body portrait of a Dinka youth (identified as Baak Kuc) wearing beaded neck ornaments and an (ivory?) arm ring. Lienhardt notes that he was "part of my entourage".
An upper body portrait of a Dinka youth wearing a beaded neck ornaments.
A portrait of an unidentified Dinka youth sitting on grass.
A group of Dinka youths sitting on the spread ashes of a cattle camp fire, with cattle and forked posts in the background.
Oxford anthropologist Godfrey Lienhardt standing with a Dinka woman who is pointing at several shrine mounds.
A line of six Dinka youths wearing European shirt and shorts. One is wearing a helmet, socks and shoes and may well have been employed by the administration.
A full length portrait of an unidentified Dinka woman in a European dress, with nose-ring and leopard-skin style slippers.

The shop in Gogrial where Oxford anthropologist Godfrey Lienhardt bought supplies during his fieldwork in the late 1940s. At the counter of the shop (owned by the Greek merchant Dimitri Yaloris) is one of his sons by his Rek Dinka wife Ayen Achom. Informants have suggested that this youth could have been one of two sons, Gregory or Vasily. [CM 10/07/2006]
A group of Dinka men dancing.
A portrait of an unidentified Dinka youth wearing European clothes sitting on a low wall outside a brick building.
View of a dance. A line of girls throw their arms forward as part of a dance movement to the left. To the right men jump and down.
View of a Dinka man dancing.
View of a large herd of Dinka cattle, moving away from a cattle camp.
Dinka village south of the Sudd region
Dinka village south of the Sudd region
View of cattle and collection of tall grass in Dinka village, south of the Sudd region
Man standing, with several people in the background
Dinka children sitting together, stacked wood in background used for Nile River steamer
Dinka children standing next to stacked wood pile, wood used as fuel for Nile River steamer
